transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-09 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Aurelia CTO), Sophie Li (Aurelia ML Eng), Tom Brooks (Aurelia PM)

[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight today, main goal is finalize model pinning for the pilot and next steps for the canary
[00:08] Rajiv Menon: sounds good Maya, hope you had the perf numbers, Sophie and I looked at last weeks run and some of the tails were weird
[00:15] Ethan Park: yeah, I ran the batch benchmarks overnight, I have the summary but quick caveat first - some transcriptions in the doc are a bit off, so i'll talk through the raw numbers.
[00:25] Sophie Li: cool, i can share the traces we captured from our staging traffic - 99th pct spikes around 1.2s on average but three spikes near 2.8s
[00:35] Ethan Park: right, so comparison: RW-13B-opt-v1.2 (float) vs RW-13B-opt-v1.3-quant (4-bit) vs third-party Mistral-7B variant. On median tokens the quant model is ~22% cheaper and latency is +10ms median but we see tail regressions in cold-cache scenarios
[00:52] Tom Brooks: by cold-cache you mean KV cache misses? we do a lot of multi-turn, so warm cache matters
[01:00] Ethan Park: exactly - warm KV cache reduces tokens and improves effective latency. The v1.3-quant path needs slightly different kernel scheduling which can amplify tail under small batch sizes; that said throughput is better for high concurrency
[01:18] Rajiv Menon: and what's the quality delta? we're sensitive in clinical summarization, can't afford hallucinations
[01:25] Ethan Park: we ran the 500 prompt eval set from last week: ROUGE-ish metrics were in line, measured QA accuracy fell by ~1.4% on v1.3-quant vs v1.2 float for our domain prompts. Some prompts with long context saw truncation artifacts, likely due to attention window handling in the quantized path
[01:42] Sophie Li: ok that's the tradeoff we expected. For the pilot, i'd rather a slightly higher cost to avoid edge-case regressions. We can explore pinning to v1.2 for a subset of routes
[01:50] Maya Patel: that's reasonable - we typically recommend a canary strategy: pin the critical endpoints (summaries, chargeback) to v1.2 float, and route less-sensitive routes to v1.3-quant to save cost. Rollbacks: automatic fallback policy to v1.2 if error rate or latency SLO breached for N minutes
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: can you define breach thresholds, like 99th pct > 2s for 5 minutes or error rate > 0.5%?
[02:18] Ethan Park: yes, we can set SLO rules in the routing layer. Recommended initial thresholds: 99th > 2.5s for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error rate > 0.7% - that'll trigger immediate rollback to pinned version and alert the oncall
[02:31] Tom Brooks: and what about canary rollout cadence? we want to ramp gradually
[02:35] Maya Patel: typical pattern: 5% traffic for 1 hour, 25% for 4 hours, 50% for 12 hours, full if stable. We can also schedule automatic rollback on the same thresholds. We'll provide a playbook
[02:49] Sophie Li: are there any gotchas around SSO or VPC peering for the private pilot? we need audit logs for SOC2 audit
[02:56] Ethan Park: audit logs are captured in the Private control plane - we can export to your SIEM. SAML SSO and RBAC mapping are supported; for VPC peering there's a config doc, I'll attach the network diagram.
[03:07] Rajiv Menon: perfect. Also curious about model pinning persistence - if we pin to v1.2 can we allow micro-updates like kernel patches but not model weights?
[03:14] Ethan Park: yes, pinning in the catalog is by model artifact hash. You can allow minor runtime/ops patches (non-weight changes) but we'll show the difference in the rollout UI. We treat weight changes as a new model version and require an explicit pin/approve
[03:26] Tom Brooks: can we have a fallback to a hosted model (eg openai) if on-prem capacity is exhausted as a last resort?
[03:33] Maya Patel: technically yes, routing policies can include external provider fallbacks, but for regulated data we recommend against sending sensitive prompts out. We can redaction or synthetic masking but we'd prefer keep in private cluster for PHI.
[03:46] Sophie Li: noted. Back to benchmarks: can you explain the tail cause again, was it the quant kernels or IO?
[03:52] Ethan Park: mostly kernel scheduling plus small-batch GPU occupancy. On short, low-concurrency traffic the quantized kernels can underutilize tensor cores causing jitter. Also context switching when KV cache cold causes additional overhead - sometimes the transcription doc said "KV cash" which was funny.
[04:08] Rajiv Menon: ha, KV cash noted. So recommended path?
[04:12] Maya Patel: recommended: pin critical routes to RW-13B-opt-v1.2 (float), route bulk conversational traffic to RW-13B-opt-v1.3-quant, run a 24h stability on v1.3-quant with your staging-like traffic, then start a canary rollout with the thresholds Ethan mentioned. If stability passes, expand pin to v1.3 for non-sensitive routes.
[04:34] Sophie Li: fine, we'll do that. Also want to capture fail-open behavior: if rollback fails for some reason, what's the last-resort?
[04:41] Ethan Park: last resort is circuit-breaker that routes to pinned float replica or blocks writes. We can also route to a degraded mode that returns cached answers for specific endpoints.
[04:52] Tom Brooks: okay that sounds good. Any infra prerequisites for the canary?
[04:56] Ethan Park: need autoscaler tuning, make sure GPU driver and cuda toolkit match the runtime we specify, and enable prefix KV caching for the long-context flows. I'll include a small checklist in the playbook.
[05:08] Maya Patel: actionables - Maya will send updated pricing, Ethan will run 24h stability and upload logs, Sophie to share failure cases and tail traces. We'll reconvene after the stability run.
[05:20] Rajiv Menon: thanks all, appreciate the clear path.
[05:23] Sophie Li: thanks, bye.
[05:25] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Notes:
- Shared artifacts: perf spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.work/perf/aurelia-pilot-2025-06), rollout playbook (will be uploaded), security docs link (https://redwood.work/security/whitepaper).
- Transcript has minor ASR errors (proper names, acronyms); see action items for owners.

End of transcript.
